questions.text: Read the passage carefully and answer the questions given below it :
questions.passage:
Education is a sub-system of the wider social system. Although it functions autonomously, it has linkage with economic, political, religious and other sub-systems which exert a powerful influence on the goals of the educational sub-systems.
Education can rarely free itself from social and cultural norms and has to relate itself to the needs of society.
Due to globalization and modernization, our society is passing through momentous changes in its value system. Values of yesteryears have taken a backseat and materialism, corruption, dishonesty and other negative values have come to the fore. At this junction, all formal and informal agencies of education like family, school and community should realize the explosiveness of the situation. It is rightly said that values cannot be taught, they are caught. All the agencies should become role models if we want our youth to be on the right path. Absence of a congenial and loving atmosphere and quarrel among parents are the major hurdles in this direction. In a nutshell, the family has ceased to be an institution for providing cultural, aesthetic and moral education.
On the other hand, formal education is squeezed between memory and mechanization. The teacher has become a businessman doing private tuition instead of institutional teaching. Race for degrees and jobs has deteriorated the situation further.
The National Policy of Education (1986) has shown concern in this regard when it says, "The growing concern over the erosion of essential values and an increasing cynicism in society has brought to focus the need for re-adjustment in the curriculum in order to make education a forceful tool for the cultivation of social and moral values."
The whole system of education needs a complete over-hauling. If at all, we the citizens are desirous of thwarting deterioration in values, teaching at all levels must emphasize on moral education and character building. Intellect without wisdom can be suicidal.

questions.text: Read the passage carefully and answer the questions given below it:
questions.passage:
The scriptures clearly define the three qualities - Tamas, Rajas and Sattva present in all of us. Tamas is inertia or resistance to transformation. Rajas is aggressiveness, restlessness or result-oriented action. Sattva is the characteristic of purity inside us.
As human beings, all of us have this quality of Sattva, which gives us patience, tolerance and establishes us in a state of utter tranquility. But our Sattvic nature has been pushed to the background. That is why we make no progress in spiritual practices like meditation. Total confusion, problems and worries are the fruits of Tamas. Lack of peace or a disturbed mind is the fruit of Rajas. Peace, happiness and contentment are the fruits of Sattva.
Our Sattvic nature is given to us in the form of energy by God himself. It empowers us to cope with problems in a very systematic way without affecting our mental peace or depleting our human qualities. It turns us to divinity and activates our Soul. Just like we preserve our food using a preservative, we should preserve our minds using the energy called Sattva. If we want to have unflagging inspiration, zeal, zest and dynamism, we have to soak our minds in Sattva.

essay_topics.name: Make notes on the above passage.
essay_topics.answer:
TITLE: Three Qualities of Mind: Tamas, Rajas and Sattva

NOTES:
1. Three Qualities in Scriptures:
   1.1 Tamas: Inertia or resistance to change; causes confusion & worries.
   1.2 Rajas: Aggressiveness & restlessness; leads to lack of peace.
   1.3 Sattva: Innate purity; brings patience, tolerance & tranquility.

2. Importance of Sattva:
   2.1 Divine energy gifted by God.
   2.2 Empowers coping with problems systematically.
   2.3 Preserves mental peace & activates the soul.

3. Preserving the Mind with Sattva:
   3.1 Mind needs Sattva just as food needs preservatives.
   3.2 Essential for inspiration, zeal, zest & dynamism.

Key to Abbreviations:
- & : and
- Qual. : qualities
- Transf. : transformation

parts.statement: Write a letter to the editor of your local newspaper, expressing your concern over the increase in the rate of road accidents, rash driving and suggesting ways to control over the accidents. Give possible solutions.
parts.explanation:
To,
The Editor,
The Daily News,
Bhopal (M.P.)

Subject: Growing concern over rash driving and road accidents.

Sir,

Through the columns of your esteemed daily, I wish to draw the attention of the authorities and the general public towards the alarming increase in road accidents caused primarily by reckless and rash driving in our city.

Over the past few months, city roads have become accident-prone zones. Drivers and motorcyclists frequently flout traffic signals, over-speed, and use mobile phones while driving. Minors riding two-wheelers without helmets have further worsened the situation, endangering the lives of innocent pedestrians and commuters.

To curb this menace, the following steps are urgently needed:
1. Stringent enforcement of traffic regulations along with heavy spot fines.
2. Installation of automated speed detection cameras at major intersections.
3. Regular sobriety checks to deter drunk driving.
4. Organizing road safety awareness campaigns in schools and colleges.

I sincerely hope that the concerned authorities will look into the matter immediately and implement preventive measures to restore road discipline.

Yours faithfully,
ABC
Resident of MP Nagar, Bhopal

questions.text: Write a paragraph in about 120 words on any one of the following topics:

parts.statement: Science and Technology
parts.explanation:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY

Science and technology are the fundamental driving forces of modern human civilization. From the invention of the wheel and electricity to modern space exploration and artificial intelligence, scientific advancements have revolutionized every walk of life. They have bridged geographical boundaries through high-speed telecommunications and modern transportation. In healthcare, cutting-edge medical technologies have eliminated deadly diseases and extended human lifespans. However, unbridled technological expansion also brings critical concerns like cybercrime, unemployment due to automation, and ecological degradation. To harness the genuine potential of science and technology, humanity must employ them ethically, ensuring that innovation always serves the collective welfare of society and nature.

parts.statement: The importance of English Language
parts.explanation:
THE IMPORTANCE OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE

English has emerged as the principal global lingua franca, connecting people across varied cultures and continents. It is the dominant medium of instruction in higher education, scientific research, international trade, diplomacy, and aviation. In today's digital era, the majority of online resources, software applications, and academic journals are documented in English. Mastery of English opens lucrative professional avenues globally and enhances interpersonal confidence. While preserving mother tongues is vital for cultural heritage, acquiring proficiency in English equips individuals with a powerful tool to excel in competitive exams, multinational careers, and international forums.

parts.statement: My Ideal Leader
parts.explanation:
MY IDEAL LEADER

My ideal leader is Mahatma Gandhi, whose philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and truth (Satya) steered India to freedom and inspired movements worldwide. A true leader does not rule by fear or authority, but guides by personal integrity, empathy, and unwavering commitment to public service. Gandhi's ascetic lifestyle and selfless dedication to uplifting the marginalized exemplify pure leadership. An ideal leader listens patiently to the voices of the citizens, remains calm in times of crisis, and prioritizes moral values over narrow self-interest. Gandhi's legacy proves that true strength lies in humility and moral conviction.

parts.statement: Online learning uses and abuses.
parts.explanation:
ONLINE LEARNING: USES AND ABUSES

Online learning has transformed education by democratizing access to quality knowledge regardless of geographical limitations. Students can access video lectures, interactive quizzes, and specialized courses anytime from home at their own pace. It offers remarkable flexibility and cost savings. Nevertheless, excessive reliance on online education carries notable drawbacks. Prolonged screen time often triggers eye fatigue, physical lethargy, and mental stress. Furthermore, access to the internet during study hours frequently leads to distractions like social media and gaming. To reap maximum benefits, online learning must be balanced with offline peer interaction and strict self-discipline.

questions.text: Fill in the blanks choosing the correct option: (any five)

parts.statement: This table is made {BLANK} wood.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: of

Explanation:
When the original material does not undergo a chemical change and remains identifiable, the preposition 'of' is used (e.g., 'made of wood').

parts.statement: Would you like to have {BLANK} tea or coffee?
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: some

Explanation:
In polite offers and requests expecting an affirmative response, 'some' is used instead of 'any'.

parts.statement: I know {BLANK} boy who cheated you.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: the

Explanation:
The definite article 'the' is used because the relative clause 'who cheated you' makes the noun 'boy' specific.

parts.statement: It {BLANK} heavily since morning.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: has been raining

Explanation:
The time preposition phrase 'since morning' indicates an action that started in the past and is still continuing, requiring the present perfect continuous tense.

parts.statement: He {BLANK} speak English fluently.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: can

Explanation:
The modal verb 'can' expresses present ability or capability.

parts.statement: Mohan is senior {BLANK} Rakesh.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: to

Explanation:
Latin comparative adjectives like senior, junior, superior, and inferior are followed by the preposition 'to', not 'than'.

parts.statement: Sunil works hard {BLANK} he may get good marks.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: so that

Explanation:
'So that' is a conjunction of purpose used before a clause containing modal verbs like 'may' or 'can'.

parts.statement: Someone is calling my name. (change the voice)
parts.explanation:
Passive Voice: My name is being called.

Explanation:
In the present continuous tense, passive voice is formed with 'is/am/are + being + V3'. Indefinite pronouns like 'someone' are omitted in the passive agent.

parts.statement: He is intelligent. He is hard working. (Combine the sentences using 'both.....and')
parts.explanation:
Combined Sentence: He is both intelligent and hard working.

Explanation:
The correlative conjunction 'both...and' joins the two coordinate adjectives describing the subject.

parts.statement: Physics is more difficult than any other subject. (Rewrite the sentence using the positive degree of the adjective used)
parts.explanation:
Rewritten Sentence: No other subject is as difficult as Physics.

Explanation:
The comparative degree 'more difficult than any other' is converted into the positive degree using 'No other...as difficult as'.

parts.statement: No sooner does a thief see a policeman than he runs away. (Rewrite the sentence using 'as soon as')
parts.explanation:
Rewritten Sentence: As soon as a thief sees a policeman, he runs away.

Explanation:
'No sooner does...than' is replaced by 'As soon as', and the inverted present tense verb form 'does...see' converts to the standard indicative form 'sees'.

parts.statement: (a) The man is our new English teacher. (b) The man is wearing a white shirt. (Combine the above simple sentences to make a complex sentence)
parts.explanation:
Combined Complex Sentence: The man who is wearing a white shirt is our new English teacher.

Explanation:
The relative clause 'who is wearing a white shirt' is embedded to form a complex sentence.

parts.statement: She shut the door. (Change into a negative sentence)
parts.explanation:
Negative Sentence: She did not shut the door.

Explanation:
'Shut' here is in the simple past tense (third person singular without '-s'), so the negative form is 'did not + shut'.

parts.statement: She is very weak. She cannot walk. (Combine the sentences using 'so......that')
parts.explanation:
Combined Sentence: She is so weak that she cannot walk.

Explanation:
'Very' is replaced by 'so', and the second clause is joined with the subordinate conjunction 'that'.

questions.text: Answer the following questions in about 30 words : (attempt any five)

parts.statement: What did Franz notice that was unusual about the school that day?
parts.explanation: Franz noticed that the school was as quiet as a Sunday morning. There was no noise of opening and closing desks or lessons repeated in unison, and village elders were sitting quietly on the back benches.

parts.statement: Mention the hazards of working in the glass bangles industry?
parts.explanation: Workers in glass bangle industries work in dingy cells without adequate light and ventilation near high-temperature furnaces. The polishing glass dust frequently blinds them, and extreme heat severely damages their health.

parts.statement: Why was the Crofter so talkative and friendly with the peddler?
parts.explanation: The crofter was an old man without a wife or child. Living in lonely isolation, he was happy and eager to have someone to converse with to overcome his loneliness.

parts.statement: How did the instructor 'build a swimmer' out of Douglas?
parts.explanation: The instructor trained Douglas step-by-step: first teaching him to breathe underwater and kick his legs using a belt and rope pulley system, and then integrating each piece into a complete swimmer.

parts.statement: What does V. S. Naipaul say about an interview?
parts.explanation: V. S. Naipaul feels that an interview causes people wounds and makes them lose a part of themselves, viewing it as an unwarranted assault on one's private individuality.

parts.statement: What were the options that Sophie was dreaming of?
parts.explanation: Sophie dreamed of opening the most boutique shop in town, becoming an actress, or taking up fashion designing, despite her family's meager financial reality.

parts.statement: When did the ironmaster realize his mistake?
parts.explanation: The ironmaster realized his mistake the following morning in broad daylight when the peddler was washed, groomed, and dressed in clean clothes, revealing he was not his old regimental comrade.

questions.text: Answer the following questions in about 30 words each: (attempt any three)

parts.statement: Why are the young trees described as 'sprinting' in the poem 'My Mother at Sixty Six'?
parts.explanation: The young sprinted trees symbolize vibrant youth, rapid passage of time, and active life, which starkly contrast with the decaying, pale, and corpse-like appearance of the poet's aging mother.

parts.statement: What can the Earth teach us Answer in light of the poem 'Keeping Quiet'?
parts.explanation: The Earth teaches us that there is life under apparent stillness. In winter, everything appears dead, but later springs back to active life, demonstrating that quiet reflection fosters rebirth.

parts.statement: What makes human beings love life in spite of troubles and sufferings?
parts.explanation: According to John Keats in 'A Thing of Beauty', some shape of beauty moves away the pall of gloom from our dark spirits, binding human beings to the lovely Earth despite grief and sorrow.

parts.statement: What was the plea of the folk who had put up the roadside stand?
parts.explanation: The rural folk pleaded for city dwellers to halt their cars and buy farm produce, hoping to earn a little city money to improve their standard of living.

questions.text: Answer any two of the following questions in about 30 words each:

parts.statement: Do you think that the third level was a medium of escape for Charley? Why?
parts.explanation: Yes, the third level was Charley's psychological escape from the stress, insecurity, fear, and modern-day anxieties of life into the peaceful, romantic world of Galesburg in 1894.

parts.statement: What did the Maharaja do to find the required number of tigers to kill?
parts.explanation: When tigers became extinct in his state, the Maharaja married a princess from a kingdom that possessed a large tiger population so that he could hunt the remaining tigers required to reach one hundred.

parts.statement: How do geological phenomena help us to know about the history of humankind?
parts.explanation: Geological formations like Antarctica preserve half-million-year-old carbon records in ice cores, helping scientists understand how continents split, climate patterns shifted, and human evolution unfolded.

questions.text: Answer any two of the following questions in about 75 words each:

parts.statement: How did Franz's feelings about M. Hamel and school change?
parts.explanation: Franz had previously dreaded going to school, fearing M. Hamel's iron ruler and having to recite participles. However, upon learning that it was M. Hamel's last French lesson due to the Prussian order, Franz's attitude changed completely. His grammar books suddenly seemed like old friends he could not bear to give up. He developed profound sympathy and deep respect for M. Hamel, forgetting his cranky nature in admiration for his four decades of dedicated service.

parts.statement: What made the peddler think that he had indeed fallen into a rat-trap?
parts.explanation: After stealing the thirty kronor from the generous crofter, the peddler avoided the public highway and walked through the forest. As night fell, he realized he had been walking in circles within the same confusing labyrinth of trees, branches, and thickets. He recognized that the thirty kronor was the bait he had taken, and the dense forest had trapped him like an inescapable rat-trap from which he could never emerge.

parts.statement: Why did Gandhiji agree to a settlement of 25 percent refund to the farmers?
parts.explanation: Gandhiji agreed to a 25 percent refund because the amount of money was less significant than the moral victory. By offering the refund, the British landlords were forced to surrender a part of their prestige along with the money. It shattered their myth of unquestioned authority, taught the Indian peasants that they had lawful rights, and infused them with the courage to resist colonial exploitation.

questions.text: Answer any one of the following questions in about 75 words:

parts.statement: What is suggested by the image 'massive weight of Uncle's Wedding band'?
parts.explanation: The phrase 'massive weight of Uncle's Wedding band' symbolizes the oppressive and burdensome nature of Aunt Jennifer's troubled marriage. Although the wedding ring itself is physically light, the marital bond carries unbearable patriarchal domination, social constraints, and emotional trauma. It signifies that she has been subjugated by the responsibilities of domestic life, losing her individual freedom, artistic autonomy, and peace of mind under male dominance.

parts.statement: Write the central idea of the poem 'My Mother at Sixty Six'.
parts.explanation: The central idea of 'My Mother at Sixty Six' by Kamala Das revolves around the painful reality of aging, mortality, and the complex bond between an aging mother and her daughter. Observing her mother's pale, corpse-like face while travelling, the poet experiences an acute ache of impending loss and separation. The poem portrays how youth contrasts with old age and concludes with the universal emotional paradox of human attachment masked behind a reassuring smile.

questions.text: Answer any one of the following questions in about 75 words :

parts.statement: Write the character sketch of Mr. Lamb.
parts.explanation: Mr. Lamb is an elderly gentleman with a tin leg, who lives in a large house with an open garden. Despite his physical handicap and children teasing him as 'Lamey-Lamb', he possesses an optimistic and warm personality. He never shuts his gates and welcomes everyone. Mr. Lamb believes in accepting life with all its imperfections, finding beauty in weeds, and enjoying the humming sound of bees. His patient and non-judgmental guidance helps Derry shed his bitter isolation and rediscover confidence in humanity.

parts.statement: Write the character sketch of Derry.
parts.explanation: Derry is a fourteen-year-old boy suffering from severe introversion and an inferiority complex caused by one side of his face being burnt by acid. Pained by the insensitive stares and pitying comments of strangers, he isolates himself and develops an abrasive and bitter attitude towards people. However, deep down, Derry craves authentic affection and companionship. His encounter with the cheerful and philosophical Mr. Lamb serves as a turning point, guiding him to overcome self-pity and look at the world with renewed hope.
